ledger.claim: The rider was at the pickup point, not absent from it. Her device recorded 36 fixes, all 36 qualifying, inside the 100 m rider-presence radius for this STANDARD zone class across the entire wait (09:10:45 to 09:16:00), stationary throughout (a single distinct speed of 0.0 kph), and the furthest of those fixes was only 44.75 m from the pin at Blk 12 Bedok South Rd. The rider-presence element of POL-NS-04 limb (c) is therefore satisfied on the trace, and nothing in the record supports the proposition that the rider had walked away from the pickup point the fee is meant to compensate for.

The waiting-window chat contains exactly one rider message and it is locating and coordinating on its face: 'im at blk 12 void deck, cant see any car, where r u?', sent 09:11:40, delivered 09:11:41, read by the driver at 09:11:55. The rider stated her own sub-location at the very block named in the pickup pin, asked for the driver's position and said she could not see the vehicle - every element POL-NS-04 limb (a) asks for. The rider did the coordinating the platform asks a rider to do.

Candour, because the judge will see it anyway: the driver did respond, and I do not press POL-NS-04 as an outright exoneration. He placed an in-app voice call at 09:12:15, 35 seconds after the rider's message, and POL-NS-04 limb (b) is drafted so that a call placed before termination answers the clause even where the call goes unanswered - this one was unanswered (answered: false, 0:18). What the record never shows is a chat reply: the rider's message sat unanswered in the chat for the full 265 seconds from 09:11:40 to the cancellation at 09:16:05. The significance of the message is therefore not the clause it fails but the fact it proves - the rider had located herself at the block on the pin and could not see the car - which leaves the RIDER_NO_SHOW code as the driver's unverified inference rather than a recorded fact.

On the admissible artifacts the record contradicts itself on rider presence and no clause resolves the conflict. The trip record terminates this trip on cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW - a recorded assertion that the rider failed to appear - while the rider's own track places her device stationary within 45 m of the same pin for the whole of the same interval. POL-NS-04 cannot break that tie because limb (b) is answered by the driver's own call, and POL-NS-03 cannot because the driver's stationary fixes lie inside the arrival radius rather than outside it. That is POL-NS-09 limb (b) precisely: two admissible artifacts in direct conflict on rider presence and no clause available to resolve it. The case should go to a human reviewer, and under POL-NS-09 the disputed $4.00 is held rather than collected while review is pending.

The two candidate dispositions are not symmetrical for this rider, and the money block says so. The $4.00 is CHARGED and no refund has issued (refund_issued_sgd 0.00, total_charged 4.00). Under POL-GEN-03, NO_ACTION is party-relative: on a rider-filed dispute it leaves the payment state exactly as it is, so the charge stands; an escalation under POL-NS-09 holds the amount instead of collecting it. Where the record leaves the rider's claim unresolved, the disposition that does not take her money pending a human decision is the escalation the record supports.

On the arrival and dwell limbs the fee survives, if it survives at all, on a 20-second margin and the driver's own marker. The derived dwell is 320 seconds measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 09:10:45 against a 300-second minimum read from platform_policy.free_wait_sec - a surplus of two sampling intervals - and the arrival marker is BUTTON, the driver's own press, so POL-NS-12's platform-confirmed arrival does not apply and POL-NS-01 limbs (b) and (c) must be established on the exported trace itself, on which the run and the dwell are the same 33 fixes and the same 320 seconds. The rider's position is that where the charge turns on 20 seconds carried by a driver-pressed marker, the strict reading of POL-NS-01 is the one to apply, and any residual doubt on that timing belongs to the reviewer under the escalation rather than to the automated pipeline resolving it in the driver's favour.
The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event for this trip, timed 2026-08-20T09:10:45+08:00, so limb (a) of the baseline chargeable no-show is satisfied on the face of the record.

The driver's own device trace puts him inside the arrival geofence for this STANDARD pickup: the trace yields 33 qualifying in-radius fixes at the 50 m STANDARD radius and the 25 m accuracy filter, carried in a single continuous run of 33 fixes beginning at 09:10:45, with a minimum recorded distance to the pickup pin of 4.25 m — comfortably more than the three consecutive in-radius fixes POL-NS-02 requires. Limb (b) of POL-NS-01 is therefore made out on the driver's own evidence.

The driver held position inside that geofence continuously for 320 seconds, running from the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 09:10:45 to the cancellation at 09:16:05, against a free waiting period of 300 seconds in force for this trip under trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec (consistent with the 300 second STANDARD minimum dwell). Limb (c) of POL-NS-01 — which measures the dwell from the first qualifying in-geofence GPS fix and not from the arrival tap — is met with 20 seconds to spare.

There is no waiting-period shortfall to excuse under POL-NS-06: the computed shortfall is minus 20 seconds, i.e. a surplus, and the trace shows a single in-geofence interval (run_count 1), so no accumulation of separate intervals is needed. The driver accordingly does not assert POL-NS-06 limb (i) and does not rely on the traffic advisory: EV-ADVIS-00406-01 is MISSING with issue code MISSING_ARTIFACT and weight_multiplier 0.0, and the driver's case stands on the trace and trip record alone, without it.

The termination limb is satisfied too: the record shows no boarding event, and the trip was terminated by the driver at 09:16:05 under cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW — one of the three reason codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises — at a moment after the 300 second dwell had elapsed at 09:15:45. The rider's own track corroborates that no boarding occurred: her device sits stationary within a maximum of 44.75 m of the pickup pin throughout the waiting window and never moves at any recorded speed above 0.0 kph.

The arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05. The first qualifying in-radius fix coincides with the arrived event at 09:10:45, so the driver was inside the 50 m STANDARD radius — not more than 300 m from the pin — at the marker's own timestamp; and no fix in the trace records a speed at or above the 15 kph motion threshold (the highest distinct speed recorded is 10.6 kph, and the trace includes stationary 0.0 kph fixes). The waiting clock was not started early, so there is nothing to recompute.

POL-NS-03 cannot displace the fee: the wrong-entrance clause applies only where the driver's stationary fixes lie outside the arrival radius but not more than 400 m from the pin, and here the qualifying fixes lie inside the 50 m STANDARD radius for the whole 320 second run. No fault allocation from the chat log arises.

POL-NS-04 does not exonerate the rider, because its limb (b) is not met. The rider's locating message was sent at 09:11:40 and the driver placed an in-app voice call recorded in trip_record.in_app_calls at 09:12:15 — 35 seconds later, and well before the 09:16:05 termination. Limb (b) requires that the driver neither replied in chat within 120 seconds nor placed an in-app call at any point before terminating; the call alone defeats it, so the clause does not apply regardless of the content of the rider's message or her position within the 100 m rider-presence radius.

The chat log is internally complete and does not impair the record: three messages are exported and trip_record.chat_message_count is 3, the msg_id sequence runs 001 to 003 without a gap, and the log spans 09:10:46 to 09:12:15 — no five minute gap straddling the arrival marker.

No impairment attaches to the artifacts that decide this case, so nothing is down-weighted and there is no escalation trigger. The trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare ledger are all COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes; the 64-point trace has 100 percent coverage, no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds; and the ledger's cancellation_fee of 4.00 SGD reconciles exactly with the platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of 4.00 for this trip, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect.

The POL-NS-07 payout is due and the anti-farming check does not withhold it: driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1 divided by completed_trips_30d of 120 gives 0.008, below the 0.08 rate — both limbs of the check must hold and neither does. The driver is therefore owed 80 percent of the 4.00 SGD fee, i.e. 3.20 SGD, the net figure computed on the ledger itself, with the residual 20 percent retained as the platform service fee.

No POL-NS-09 escalation limb is engaged: the anti-farming check does not trip, rider_profile.no_show_disputes_30d is 0, and rider_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d and driver_profile.disputes_with_counterparty_90d are both 0, so there are no repeat disputes between these parties in the trailing window. No admissible artifact contradicts another on arrival, dwell or rider presence, and with every deciding artifact at weight 1.0 the confidence floor is not breached.

All four conditions of POL-NS-01 hold and none of POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces them, so the cancellation fee of 4.00 SGD stands and the rider's refund claim fails; the case produces the outcome POL-NS-07 fixes — DRIVER_COMPENSATION of 3.20 SGD to the driver, with amount_sgd mirroring driver_compensation_sgd, the rider's charge standing as recorded in the ledger.

ruling.explanation:
This ruling decides the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-00406. The fee stands, and the driver is paid SGD 3.20.

WHY THE FEE STANDS. POL-NS-01 makes a no-show fee chargeable only where four conditions all hold, and they do. (a) The trip record (EV-TRIP-00406) carries a driver 'arrived' event at 09:10:45. (b) The driver's own device trace (EV-GPS-00406) places him inside the 50 m STANDARD arrival radius from 09:10:45 — 33 consecutive qualifying fixes under the 25 m accuracy filter, the closest 4.25 m from the pin. (c) He held position inside that geofence for 320 continuous seconds, from 09:10:45 to the cancellation at 09:16:05, against the 300-second free waiting period in force on the trip record (platform_policy.free_wait_sec, 300 s) — a surplus of 20 seconds. (d) No boarding event is recorded and the trip was terminated by the driver at 09:16:05 under RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three reason codes limb (d) recognises, at or after the moment the 300 seconds elapsed at 09:15:45. The arrival marker is the driver's own button, not a GPS_AUTO arrival, so POL-NS-12 assists neither party — but the arrival and the dwell are established on the exported trace itself (100 per cent coverage, 64 fixes, no gap, single 33-fix run), which is the strict reading the rider asks for. POL-NS-06 does not apply: the derived shortfall is minus 20 seconds, i.e., a surplus. POL-NS-03 does not apply: it governs drivers stationary outside the arrival radius but within 400 m of the pin, and the driver's fixes here are inside the radius. The ledger's cancellation-fee line of SGD 4.00 reconciles with platform_policy.cancellation_fee_sgd of SGD 4.00, so there is no POL-NS-08(d) fare defect and no mis-selected reason code to refer.

TO THE RIDER. I accept both of your factual points. Your message at 09:11:40 ('im at blk 12 void deck, cant see any car, where r u?') is a properly locating message, and your own track (EV-GPS-00406 rider_presence) puts your device stationary within 45 m of the pin for the whole window. Neither of those refunds the fee. The clause that converts a present, coordinating rider into a refund is POL-NS-04, and it fails its limb (b): that limb requires the driver neither to have replied in chat within 120 seconds nor to have placed an in-app call before terminating. He placed an in-app call at 09:12:15, 35 seconds after your message — 18 seconds, unanswered, recorded on the trip record (in_app_calls). The clause is drafted so that a call answers it whether or not it is picked up, and that is why your presence and your message, though true, do not exonerate you. Your argument that RIDER_NO_SHOW is the driver's 'unverified inference' does not defeat limb (d): the clause reads the recorded cancellation reason code as its own test, the code is one of the three it recognises, and it was set after the waiting period had run.

ON YOUR ESCALATION ARGUMENT (POL-NS-09(b)). You ask for a holding — a direct conflict between admissible artifacts on arrival, dwell or rider presence that no clause resolves. There is none. The trip record and the trace agree on arrival and on dwell. The RIDER_NO_SHOW value is a reason the driver recorded, not a measurement of where you were, and POL-NS-01(d) takes that recorded code as its test; it is satisfied. The question your presence raises — whether POL-NS-04 exonerates you — is answered by that clause, and answered no, because of the call. A conflict the policy's own clause resolves is not the unresolved conflict POL-NS-09(b) describes, so the fee is not held and I do not escalate. Your related point that NO_ACTION leaves the SGD 4.00 charge in place while escalation would hold it is correct as far as it goes, but it only matters if the case is genuinely unresolved, and it is not.

TO THE DRIVER. Your account — that you called when you saw the message and waited the full time — is consistent with the chat log (EV-CHAT-00406: your call at 09:12:15, cancellation at 09:16:05) and with the trace. Under POL-NS-07 you are paid 80 per cent of the SGD 4.00 fee, SGD 3.20, the net figure the ledger itself computes (EV-FARE-00406, driver_compensation 3.20), the residual SGD 0.20 being retained as the platform service fee. The anti-farming check does not withhold it: your no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the 4 the clause requires, and 1 divided by 120 completed trips in 30 days is 0.008, below the 0.08 rate; both limbs must hold, and neither does (EV-DPROF-00406). Because compensation is paid, the ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION and amount_sgd mirrors driver_compensation_sgd at SGD 3.20; the rider's charge stands as recorded.

WEIGHT AND CONFIDENCE. Every artifact carrying a deciding fact — the trip record, the GPS trace, the fare ledger and the chat log — is COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issue codes, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0. The traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00406-01 is MISSING at weight 0.0, but nothing rests on it: POL-NS-06 limb (i) accumulation is unavailable and unnecessary because there is no shortfall. No artifact below weight 1.0 carries any finding. Confidence is 0.95. The monetary effect, SGD 3.20, is below the SGD 8.00 execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so the ruling executes on issue, subject to appeal under POL-GEN-04.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and every draft agreed on this ruling, so it is carried unanimously (vote agreement 1.00).
